Working Directory (setwd)

Best programming practice is to avoid setwd() in analysis code: it hardcodes an assumption about the working directory (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine), so the code breaks when run anywhere else. Keep the working directory as the caller sets it and use relative paths. setwd() calls were found in 2 code files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). No install.packages() calls were found in any of the code files.

This module runs automated data-quality checks (empty columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, stray whitespace, numbers stored as text, problematic and colliding column names, mixed text encodings, personal information, spreadsheet formatting, and careless responding) on the extracted data files.

We examined 1528 columns across 142 data files.

Issues Identified

4 file/column combinations have at least one issue.

File Column Issues
p36imp_osf_bundle_20261007_v5.zip/osf_bundle/results/variants_b3_0.0_MAR.csv rel_bias ⬜ Empty column — Column is empty: all 48 values are missing
p36imp_osf_bundle_20261007_v5.zip/osf_bundle/results/variants_b3_0.0_MCAR.csv rel_bias ⬜ Empty column — Column is empty: all 48 values are missing
p36imp_osf_bundle_paper1_2026-10-27_2044_56f9ba37.zip/osf_bundle/results/variants_b3_0.0_MAR.csv rel_bias ⬜ Empty column — Column is empty: all 48 values are missing
p36imp_osf_bundle_paper1_2026-10-27_2044_56f9ba37.zip/osf_bundle/results/variants_b3_0.0_MCAR.csv rel_bias ⬜ Empty column — Column is empty: all 48 values are missing

Careless Responding

No file could be screened for careless responding.

What this does not cover. Only 0 of 142 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

We ran the paper’s 92 R scripts and 90 Python scripts in the order they depend on each other, each in an isolated container, for at most 5 minutes per script. 128 identical copies of these scripts, which other links in the paper lead to, were not run again.

File paths

7 data paths in the code do not work in the repository as deposited. We pointed them to where the file is, so the code could run: simulation_functions.R to R/simulation_functions.R (in run_mi_variants.R); simulation_functions.R to R/simulation_functions.R (in aggregate_from_raw.R); simulation_functions.R to R/simulation_functions.R (in p36_smcfcs_vs_custom_2026-10-22.R); disagrees with results/quadratic_kappa_curve.csv to ../p36p3_osf_deposit/results/quadratic_kappa_curve.csv (in fig_moment_defect_structure.R); summary.csv to results/summary.csv (in make_figure.R); simulation_functions.R to R/simulation_functions.R (in make_intuition_figures.R); simulation_functions.R to R/simulation_functions.R (in run_simulation.R). The code should be changed, because as written it does not find these files. The code reads files that are only inside p36imp_osf_bundle_paper1_2026-10-27_2044_56f9ba37.zip, p36p2_osf-deposit_2026-11-09_1850_9c8b71dc.zip, p36p3_osf-deposit_2026-11-12_1303_beb9d6d2.zip, p36p2_osf-deposit_2026-11-14_2210_62c85d9d.zip, p36p3_osf-deposit_2026-11-16_0651_efa5c1da.zip, p36imp_osf_bundle_20261007_v5.zip, and no script unpacks them. We unpacked them in their folder before the run. So that others can run the code as deposited, start the code with a line that unpacks them (such as unzip("p36imp_osf_bundle_paper1_2026-10-27_2044_56f9ba37.zip") in R), or upload the files unpacked. 72 references matched several files sharing a name and could not be resolved by study group or folder; they were left unrewritten and flagged. 196 data paths were built at runtime with sprintf()/paste()/file.path() instead of written as a literal path — this is fragile authoring practice (it silently breaks if the code is run from a different working directory than the author’s own). We resolved all of these on a best-effort basis.

Execution

The code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 98 scripts: 53 ran without error, 7 errored, 6 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse, and 6 were run by another script with source(). Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions. 26 scripts were not started, or stopped early, because the time for all scripts together had run out.

> cov2 <- function(lambda, w) pnorm(w * (1 - lambda)) - pnorm(-w * (1 + lambda))
> rows <- list()
> k <- 0L
> for (f in c("variants_b3_0.4_MAR", "variants_b3_0.4_MCAR", "variants_b3_0.0_MAR")) {
>   d <- read.csv(sprintf("results/%s.csv", f))
>   bias <- if (grepl("0.0", f)) d$mean_est else d$bias   # null design: truth is 0
>   h <- d$ci_width / 2
>   k <- k + 1L
>   rows[[k]] <- data.frame(source = f, method = d$method, N = d$N, rate = d$rate,
>                           bias = bias, empSE = d$empSE, h = h,
>                           lambda = bias / h, w = h / d$empSE,
>                           observed = d$coverage, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
> }
> D <- do.call(rbind, rows)
> D <- D[is.finite(D$lambda) & is.finite(D$w), ]
> D$predicted <- cov2(D$lambda, D$w)
> D$resid <- D$observed - D$predicted

>     for (a in draw_order) {
>       ss <- d[d$method == a & d$rate == r, ]
>       ss <- ss[order(ss$N), ]
>       if (!nrow(ss)) next
>       cfg <- arms[[a]]
>       lines(ss$N, ss[[m$v]], col = cfg$col, lwd = cfg$lwd)
>       # THIRD instance of the same bug in this repo: whiskers drawn before the
>       # line at lwd 1.1 and 45% opacity, in the line's own hue, so an opaque
>       # lwd 3.0 line covered them and the footer promised something invisible.
>       # Already fixed in fig_sequel_grid.R and fig_sequel_kappa_curve.R. On top,
>       # opaque, capped -- and the caps matter most here, where six arms overlap.
>       lo_i <- ss[[m$v]] - ss[[m$mc]]; hi_i <- ss[[m$v]] + ss[[m$mc]]
>       segments(ss$N, lo_i, ss$N, hi_i, col = cfg$col,
>                lwd = if (cfg$key) 1.5 else 1.0)
>       segments(ss$N * 0.985, lo_i, ss$N * 1.015, lo_i, col = cfg$col,
>                lwd = if (cfg$key) 1.5 else 1.0)
>       segments(ss$N * 0.985, hi_i, ss$N * 1.015, hi_i, col = cfg$col,
>                lwd = if (cfg$key) 1.5 else 1.0)
>       points(ss$N, ss[[m$v]], pch = 16, cex = if (cfg$key) .8 else .55,
>              col = cfg$col)
>       if (cfg$key) ends[[a]] <- list(y = ss[[m$v]][nrow(ss)], cfg = cfg)
>     }
>     # ---- de-collide the right-edge labels, then draw them ---------------
>     if (length(ends)) {
>       ys  <- vapply(ends, function(e) e$y, numeric(1))
>       ord <- order(ys)
>       # The separation used to be a flat 5.5% of the panel's data range, a
>       # number with no relation to how tall the type actually is. At the size
>       # the labels print it came to about 3 points for a 9-point label, so in
>       # the null figure's Type I error panel four labels ran into each other --
>       # "Regression imp." dropping its p into the ascenders of "Mean imp."
>       #
>       # Two things had to change, and the second is the one that is easy to get
>       # wrong. (1) The labels are anchored on their BASELINE, adj = c(0, 0),
>       # not on their vertical centre. With centre anchoring R places each
>       # string on a metric box that does not include the same parts of the
>       # glyphs for every string -- measured on this device, "Regression imp."
>       # set bold and "MI-JAV" set regular land their ink nearly six points
>       # apart relative to the same anchor -- so a separation computed from
>       # strheight() leaves one printed pixel between them. On the baseline they
>       # behave like ordinary lines of text. (2) The separation is a LINE PITCH,
>       # 1.28 line-heights of the largest label, which is what typesetting a
>       # paragraph would use. Measured on this device that leaves 2.8 points of
>       # white between the closest pair; strheight() left 0.3.
>       e_ord <- ends[ord]
>       lcex  <- vapply(e_ord, function(e)
>                  if (e$cfg$key) lab_cex[["key"]] else lab_cex[["ref"]], numeric(1))
>       pitch <- 1.28 * 12 * max(lcex) / 72 *
>                diff(par("usr")[3:4]) / par("pin")[2]
>       yl    <- ys[ord]
>       for (i in seq_along(yl)[-1])
>         if (yl[i] - yl[i-1] < pitch) yl[i] <- yl[i-1] + pitch
>       # re-centre the stack on the original span, then hold it inside the
>       # panel: without the clamp a bunched stack walks out of the top or
>       # bottom and prints over the panel above or the axis below.
>       shift <- mean(ys) - mean(yl); yl <- yl + shift
>       bot <- ylim[1] + 0.15 * pitch; top <- ylim[2] - 0.85 * pitch
>       if (diff(range(yl)) <= top - bot) {
>         if (max(yl) > top) yl <- yl - (max(yl) - top)
>         if (min(yl) < bot) yl <- yl + (bot - min(yl))
>       } else {                 # six labels taller than the panel: centre them
>         yl <- seq(0, by = pitch, length.out = length(yl))
>         yl <- yl - mean(yl) + mean(c(bot, top))
>       }
>       for (i in seq_along(ord)) {
>         e <- ends[[ord[i]]]
>         # leader line from the series end to its (moved) label
>         # the leader points at the middle of the label, not at its baseline
>         segments(max(Ns) * 1.02, e$y, max(Ns) * 1.085, yl[i] + 0.30 * pitch,
>                  xpd = NA, col = adjustcolor(e$cfg$col, .5), lwd = .8)
>         text(max(Ns) * 1.125, yl[i], e$cfg$lab, adj = c(0, 0), xpd = NA,
>              cex = if (e$cfg$key) lab_cex[["key"]] else lab_cex[["ref"]],
>              col = if (e$cfg$key) e$cfg$col else grey,
>              font = if (e$cfg$key) 2 else 1)
>       }
>     }
>     # The reference value used to be printed at min(Ns) in every panel. That is
>     # fine on the bias panels and collides badly on the coverage panels, where
>     # the arms straddle 0.95 at exactly that x. Trying to place it in the
>     # clearest gap did not help either, and the reason is worth stating: on a
>     # coverage panel the well-behaved arms sit ON the reference line by design,
>     # so no clear gap exists anywhere along it.
>     #
>     # It is also redundant there -- the panel is titled "95% CI coverage" and
>     # 0.95 is an axis tick. So label the line only when the axis does not
>     # already say what it is, which leaves the 0.05 of the Type I error panel
>     # labelled and drops the rest.
>     if (!is.na(m$ref) && !any(abs(axTicks(2) - m$ref) < 1e-9))
>       text(min(Ns), m$ref, sprintf("%.2f", m$ref), pos = 3, offset = .25,
>            cex = .70, col = grey)
>   }
> }
> mtext(ttl, side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 1.0, cex = 1.06, font = 2, col = ink)
> par(fig = c(0, 1, 0, 1), oma = c(0, 0, 0, 0), mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), new = TRUE)

> zeta_plim <- function(rho1, rho2, pi_t, gy = 0.7, nref = 4e6) {
>   # selection moments from a large reference draw of Y ~ N(0,1)
>   y  <- rnorm(nref)
>   g0 <- uniroot(function(a) mean(plogis(a + gy * y)) - pi_t, c(-30, 30))$root
>   R  <- runif(nref) >= plogis(g0 + gy * y)          # TRUE = observed
>   p_o <- mean(R); p_m <- 1 - p_o
>   m1_o <- mean(y[R]);  m2_o <- mean(y[R]^2)
>   m1_m <- mean(y[!R]); m2_m <- mean(y[!R]^2)
>   v_o  <- m2_o - m1_o^2
>   A <- p_o * m2_o; B <- p_m * m2_m
> 
>   b   <- (rho1 + rho2) / 2                          # pooled slope
>   rr  <- c(rho1, rho2)
>   s2  <- mean(rr^2 * v_o + 1 - rr^2) - b^2 * v_o    # pooled residual variance
> 
>   r_g <- vapply(rr, function(rho) {
>     k    <- (rho - b) * m1_o
>     cov  <- rho * A + b * B + k * p_m * m1_m
>     ex   <- p_o * rho * m1_o + p_m * (k + b * m1_m)
>     ex2  <- p_o * (rho^2 * m2_o + 1 - rho^2) +
>             p_m * (k^2 + 2 * k * b * m1_m + b^2 * m2_m + s2)
>     cov / sqrt(ex2 - ex^2)
>   }, numeric(1))
>   atanh(r_g[1]) - atanh(r_g[2])
> }
> zeta_sim <- function(rho1, rho2, pi_t, gy = 0.7, N = 4e6) {
>   n1 <- N / 2
>   G  <- rep(1:2, each = n1)
>   rho <- ifelse(G == 1, rho1, rho2)
>   y  <- rnorm(N)
>   x  <- rho * y + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * rnorm(N)
>   g0 <- uniroot(function(a) mean(plogis(a + gy * y)) - pi_t, c(-30, 30))$root
>   mis <- runif(N) < plogis(g0 + gy * y)
>   fit <- lm(x[!mis] ~ y[!mis] + factor(G[!mis]))    # POOLED slope, group main effect
>   cf  <- coef(fit); s <- sigma(fit)
>   xs  <- x
>   km  <- cf[1] + ifelse(G[mis] == 2, cf[3], 0)
>   xs[mis] <- km + cf[2] * y[mis] + s * rnorm(sum(mis))
>   r1 <- cor(xs[G == 1], y[G == 1]); r2 <- cor(xs[G == 2], y[G == 2])
>   atanh(r1) - atanh(r2)
> }

> GZY <- 0.7
> ols <- function(y, X) {                    # coefficients + residual variance
>   b <- solve(crossprod(X), crossprod(X, y))
>   r <- y - X %*% b
>   list(b = as.numeric(b), s2 = sum(r^2) / length(y))
> }
> run_one <- function(b3, observed_only, seed = 20261002L) {
>   set.seed(seed)
>   z1 <- rnorm(N); z2 <- rnorm(N)
>   X1 <- z1; X2 <- RHO * z1 + sqrt(1 - RHO^2) * z2
>   Y  <- B1 * X1 + B2 * X2 + b3 * X1 * X2 + rnorm(N, 0, SIG)
> 
>   # The mechanism, z-scored on this sample's own moments and calibrated
>   # so the expected missing rate is RATE -- as calibrate_mar() does.
>   eta <- GZ2 * (X2 - mean(X2)) / sd(X2) + GZY * (Y - mean(Y)) / sd(Y)
>   g0  <- uniroot(function(g) mean(plogis(g + eta)) - RATE, c(-20, 20),
>                  tol = 1e-12)$root
>   mis <- runif(N) < plogis(g0 + eta)
>   obs <- !mis
> 
>   # Initialize exactly as impute_smc_draw() does.
>   x1 <- X1; x1[mis] <- NA
>   init <- ols(X1[obs], cbind(1, X2[obs], Y[obs]))$b
>   x1[mis] <- init[1] + init[2] * X2[mis] + init[3] * Y[mis]
> 
>   trace <- matrix(NA_real_, ITERS, 2,

> draw_params <- function(y, x) {
>   # The covariate model is drawn from its posterior alongside the substantive
>   # one: the mean from its normal posterior given the variance, the variance from
>   # a scaled inverse-chi-squared. Nothing here touches the generating law.
>   n  <- length(x)
>   s2x <- sum((x - mean(x))^2) / rchisq(1, n - 1)
>   mx <- mean(x) + rnorm(1) * sqrt(s2x / n)
>   Z <- cbind(1, x, x^2)
>   qrZ <- qr(Z); bhat <- qr.coef(qrZ, y)
>   r <- y - Z %*% bhat
>   df <- length(y) - ncol(Z)
>   s2 <- sum(r^2) / rchisq(1, df)                       # scaled inverse-chi^2
>   V  <- chol2inv(qr.R(qrZ))                            # (Z'Z)^-1
>   bet <- as.numeric(bhat) + as.numeric(t(chol(V)) %*% rnorm(3)) * sqrt(s2)
>   list(b0 = bet[1], b1 = bet[2], b2 = bet[3], s = sqrt(s2),
>        mx = mx, sx = sqrt(s2x))
> }

> .gmom <- function(mu, sd, a, gy, k, missing) {
>   f <- function(y) {

>     y^k * dnorm(y, mu, sd) * (if (missing) w else 1 - w)
>   }

> expit <- function(z) 1 / (1 + exp(-z))

> sel <- function(pi_t, gam = gY) {
>   if (gam == 0) {
>     return(list(po = 1 - pi_t, pm = pi_t, m1o = 0, m2o = 1, m1m = 0, m2m = 1,
>                 A = 1 - pi_t, B = pi_t))
>   }
>   g0 <- uniroot(function(g) I1(function(y) dnorm(y) * expit(g + gam * y)) - pi_t,
>                 c(-40, 40), tol = 1e-14)$root
>   w  <- function(y) expit(g0 + gam * y)
>   pm <- I1(function(y) dnorm(y) * w(y)); po <- 1 - pm
>   list(po = po, pm = pm,
>        m1o = I1(function(y) y * dnorm(y) * (1 - w(y))) / po,
>        m2o = I1(function(y) y^2 * dnorm(y) * (1 - w(y))) / po,
>        m1m = I1(function(y) y * dnorm(y) * w(y)) / pm,
>        m2m = I1(function(y) y^2 * dnorm(y) * w(y)) / pm,
>        A   = I1(function(y) y^2 * dnorm(y) * (1 - w(y))),
>        B   = I1(function(y) y^2 * dnorm(y) * w(y)))
> }
> cov_star <- function(s, r) {

> }

> MEASURE <- 6.5
> fold <- function(s) { Encoding(s) <- "UTF-8"; gsub("[^ -~]", "n", s, perl = TRUE) }
> wrap_lines <- function(txt) {
>   txt <- fold(txt)
>   words <- strsplit(txt, "[ \t]+")[[1]]
>   words <- words[nzchar(words)]
>   if (!length(words)) return(0L)
>   n <- 1L; cur <- ""
>   for (w in words) {
>     cand <- if (nzchar(cur)) paste(cur, w) else w
>     if (strwidth(cand, units = "inches") > MEASURE) { n <- n + 1L; cur <- w }
>     else cur <- cand
>   }
>   n
> }
> count_lines <- function(path, from, to) {
>   x <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8")
>   a <- grep(from, x, fixed = TRUE)[1]
>   b <- if (is.null(to)) length(x) else {
>     hit <- grep(to, x, fixed = TRUE); if (length(hit)) hit[1] - 1L else length(x)
>   }
>   seg <- x[a:b]
> 
>   # Drop HTML comments: internal notes, not submitted text.
>   txt <- paste(seg, collapse = "\n")
>   txt <- gsub("(?s)<!--.*?-->", "", txt, perl = TRUE)
>   seg <- strsplit(txt, "\n")[[1]]
> 
>   lines <- 0L; words <- 0L
>   i <- 1L
>   while (i <= length(seg)) {
>     ln <- seg[i]
>     if (!nzchar(trimws(ln))) { i <- i + 1L; next }
> 
>     # A table row occupies at least one typeset line; separator rows do not.
>     if (grepl("^\\s*\\|", ln)) {
>       if (!grepl("^\\s*\\|[-: |]*\\|\\s*$", ln)) {
>         lines <- lines + 1L
>         words <- words + length(strsplit(trimws(ln), "\\s+")[[1]])
>       }
>       i <- i + 1L; next
>     }
> 
>     # Headings and list items each start their own line.
>     if (grepl("^#", ln) || grepl("^\\s*([-*]|[0-9]+\\.)\\s", ln)) {
>       s <- gsub("^#+\\s*|^\\s*([-*]|[0-9]+\\.)\\s*", "", ln)
>       s <- gsub("\\*\\*|\\*|`", "", s)
>       lines <- lines + wrap_lines(s)
>       words <- words + length(strsplit(trimws(s), "\\s+")[[1]])
>       i <- i + 1L; next
>     }
> 
>     # Otherwise gather the soft-wrapped paragraph and wrap it as one block.
>     para <- character()
>     while (i <= length(seg) && nzchar(trimws(seg[i])) &&
>            !grepl("^#|^\\s*\\||^\\s*([-*]|[0-9]+\\.)\\s", seg[i])) {
>       para <- c(para, seg[i]); i <- i + 1L
>     }
>     s <- gsub("\\*\\*|\\*|`", "", paste(para, collapse = " "))
>     lines <- lines + wrap_lines(s)
>     words <- words + length(strsplit(trimws(s), "\\s+")[[1]])
>   }
>   c(lines = lines, words = words)
> }

> set.seed(20260801L)
> B1 <- 0.3
> B2 <- 0.4
> SIG <- 1.0
> GAMMA1 <- 0.7
> gen <- function(n) {
>   X <- rnorm(n)
>   data.frame(X = X, Y = B1 * X + B2 * X^2 + rnorm(n, sd = SIG))
> }
> mar_intercept <- function(target, n = 2e5) {
>   d <- gen(n); z <- as.numeric(scale(d$Y))
>   uniroot(function(g0) mean(plogis(g0 + GAMMA1 * z)) - target, c(-12, 12))$root
> }
> impute_joint <- function(x, w, y) {
>   o  <- !is.na(x)
>   Z  <- cbind(1, y)
>   Zo <- Z[o, , drop = FALSE]; Zm <- Z[!o, , drop = FALSE]
>   Yo <- cbind(x[o], w[o])
>   XtXinv <- chol2inv(chol(crossprod(Zo)))
>   Bhat <- XtXinv %*% crossprod(Zo, Yo)
>   E    <- Yo - Zo %*% Bhat
>   S    <- crossprod(E)
>   df   <- nrow(Zo) - ncol(Zo)
>   Sinv <- chol2inv(chol(S))
>   Sig  <- chol2inv(chol(rWishart(1, df, Sinv)[, , 1]))    # inverse-Wishart
>   B    <- Bhat + t(chol(XtXinv)) %*%
>           matrix(rnorm(4), 2, 2) %*% chol(Sig)            # matrix normal
>   nm   <- nrow(Zm)
>   Zm %*% B + matrix(rnorm(nm * 2), nm, 2) %*% chol(Sig)
> }
> GRID <- seq(-5, 5, length.out = 401)
> impute_smc <- function(y_mis, b1, b2, s, chunk = 20000L) {
>   out <- numeric(length(y_mis))
>   lp  <- dnorm(GRID, log = TRUE)
>   for (a in seq(1, length(y_mis), by = chunk)) {
>     b   <- min(a + chunk - 1L, length(y_mis))
>     yy  <- y_mis[a:b]
>     mu  <- outer(rep(1, length(yy)), b1 * GRID + b2 * GRID^2)
>     dev <- (yy - mu)
>     lw  <- sweep(-dev^2 / (2 * s^2), 2, lp, "+")
>     # Categorical draw by Gumbel-max rather than inverse-CDF. The first version
>     # used t(apply(W, 1, cumsum)), an R-level loop over 20,000 rows per chunk
>     # run several hundred times, which took the script from an estimated few
>     # minutes to over twenty and still had a cell to go. Gumbel-max is exact,
>     # needs no normalisation and no cumulative sum, and is shift-invariant per
>     # row so the max-subtraction is unnecessary too.
>     g   <- -log(-log(matrix(runif(length(lw)), nrow(lw), ncol(lw))))
>     idx <- max.col(lw + g, ties.method = "first")
>     # jitter within the grid cell so the draw is continuous, not lattice-valued
>     out[a:b] <- GRID[idx] + runif(length(yy), -1, 1) * (GRID[2] - GRID[1]) / 2
>   }
>   out
> }

>   "Listwise"      = function(df) m_listwise(df, true = b3_true),
>   "Mean imp."     = function(df) m_mean(df, true = b3_true),
>   "Regression imp." = function(df) m_regression(df, true = b3_true),
>   "MI-naive"      = function(df) m_mi_naive(df, true = b3_true, m = 20),
>   "MI-JAV"        = function(df) m_mi_jav(df, true = b3_true, m = 20),
>   "MI-SMC"        = function(df) m_mi(df, true = b3_true, m = 20)
> )
> acc <- lapply(methods, function(f) {
>   list(est = numeric(0), cov = numeric(0), width = numeric(0), rej = numeric(0),
>        fail = 0L)
> })
> realized_miss <- numeric(reps)
> for (r in seq_len(reps)) {
>   df <- impose_mar()
>   realized_miss[r] <- mean(is.na(df$X1))
>   for (nm in names(methods)) {
>     out <- tryCatch(methods[[nm]](df), error = function(e) NULL)
>     if (is.null(out) || any(!is.finite(out[c("est", "ci_lo", "ci_hi")]))) {
>       acc[[nm]]$fail <- acc[[nm]]$fail + 1L
>       next
>     }
>     acc[[nm]]$est   <- c(acc[[nm]]$est, out["est"])
>     acc[[nm]]$cov   <- c(acc[[nm]]$cov, out["covered"])
>     acc[[nm]]$width <- c(acc[[nm]]$width, out["ci_hi"] - out["ci_lo"])
>     acc[[nm]]$rej   <- c(acc[[nm]]$rej, out["reject"])
>   }
> }

> suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(source("R/simulation_functions.R")))
> set.seed(2607)
> rho1 <- 0.6
> rho2 <- 0.2
> pi_t <- 0.40
> gy <- 0.7
> N <- 400
> OI <- list(blue = "#0072B2", verm = "#D55E00", ink = "#1a1a1a",
>            grey = "#8a8a8a", faint = "#d9d9d9")
> n1 <- N/2
> G   <- rep(1:2, each = n1)
> rho <- ifelse(G == 1, rho1, rho2)
> y   <- rnorm(N)
> x   <- rho * y + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * rnorm(N)
> g0  <- uniroot(function(a) mean(plogis(a + gy * rnorm(2e5))) - pi_t, c(-30, 30))$root
> mis <- runif(N) < plogis(g0 + gy * y)
> fp  <- lm(x[!mis] ~ y[!mis] + factor(G[!mis]))
> b_p <- coef(fp)[2]
> s_p <- sigma(fp)
> xp  <- x
> xp[mis] <- coef(fp)[1] + ifelse(G[mis] == 2, coef(fp)[3], 0) +
>            b_p * y[mis] + s_p * rnorm(sum(mis))
> xg <- x
> slopes_g <- numeric(2)
> for (gg in 1:2) {
>   idx <- G == gg; obs <- idx & !mis; mm <- idx & mis
>   f <- lm(x[obs] ~ y[obs]); slopes_g[gg] <- coef(f)[2]
>   xg[mm] <- coef(f)[1] + coef(f)[2] * y[mm] + sigma(f) * rnorm(sum(mm))
> }
> zof <- function(v) atanh(cor(v[G==1], y[G==1])) - atanh(cor(v[G==2], y[G==2]))
> z_full <- zof(x)
> z_pool <- zof(xp)
> z_grp <- zof(xg)
> png("results/sequel_mech_slopes.png", width = 1873, height = 807, res = 288)
> layout(matrix(c(1,2,3,4,4,4), 2, 3, byrow = TRUE), heights = c(3.1, 1))
> par(family = "sans", col.axis = OI$ink, fg = OI$ink, cex.axis = .76)
> panel <- function(xv, ttl, sub, imputed_open, show_pooled = FALSE) {
>   par(mar = c(2.9, 2.9, 3.4, 0.6))
>   plot(NA, xlim = c(-3, 3), ylim = c(-3.2, 3.2), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
>   abline(h = 0, v = 0, col = OI$faint, lwd = 1, lty = 3)
>   for (gg in 1:2) {
>     col <- if (gg == 1) OI$blue else OI$verm
>     idx <- G == gg
>     # observed = filled, imputed = open
>     points(y[idx & !mis], xv[idx & !mis], pch = 19, cex = .5,
>            col = adjustcolor(col, .55))
>     if (imputed_open)
>       points(y[idx & mis], xv[idx & mis], pch = 21, cex = .55,
>              col = col, bg = "white", lwd = .9)
>     f <- lm(xv[idx] ~ y[idx])
>     abline(f, col = col, lwd = 2.6)
>   }
>   if (show_pooled) {                      # the single slope used to fill BOTH groups
>     abline(a = coef(fp)[1], b = b_p, col = OI$ink, lwd = 1.8, lty = 2)
>     text(-2.9, 2.65, "one pooled slope\nfills both groups", adj = 0, cex = .62,
>          col = OI$ink)
>   }
>   axis(1, lwd = 0, lwd.ticks = .8, col.ticks = OI$grey)
>   axis(2, las = 1, lwd = 0, lwd.ticks = .8, col.ticks = OI$grey)
>   mtext("Y", side = 1, line = 1.8, cex = .76)
>   mtext("X", side = 2, line = 1.8, cex = .76)
>   mtext(ttl, side = 3, line = 1.9, adj = 0, cex = .86, col = OI$ink)
>   for (i in seq_along(sub))
>     mtext(sub[i], side = 3, line = 1.0 - 0.85 * (i - 1), adj = 0,
>           cex = .66, col = OI$grey)
> }
> panel(x,  "A. Complete data",        "two genuinely different slopes", FALSE)
> panel(xp, "B. Pooled imputation",    c("one slope fills both groups", "-> gap closes"), TRUE, TRUE)

> source("R/simulation_functions.R")
> set.seed(20260804L + 313L)
> N <- 5e5
> M <- 5L
> PI <- 0.40
> REPS <- 24L
> GAMMA1 <- 0.7
> predictors <- function(b1, b2, s) {
>   VarY <- b1^2 + 2 * b2^2 + s^2
>   c(rho2 = b1^2 / VarY,
>     r    = (b1 / VarY)^2 * (8 * b2^3 + 6 * b1^2 * b2) / (2 * b2))
> }
> mar_intercept <- function(b1, b2, s, target, n = 2e5) {
>   x <- rnorm(n); y <- b1 * x + b2 * x^2 + rnorm(n, sd = s)
>   z <- as.numeric(scale(y))
>   uniroot(function(g0) mean(plogis(g0 + GAMMA1 * z)) - target, c(-12, 12))$root
> }
> kappa_at <- function(b1, b2, sig, mech = c("MAR", "MCAR"), reps = REPS) {
>   mech <- match.arg(mech)
>   g0 <- if (mech == "MAR") mar_intercept(b1, b2, sig, PI) else NA_real_
>   k <- numeric(reps)
>   for (rep in seq_len(reps)) {
>     X <- rnorm(N); Y <- b1 * X + b2 * X^2 + rnorm(N, sd = sig)
>     miss <- if (mech == "MAR")
>       runif(N) < plogis(g0 + GAMMA1 * as.numeric(scale(Y))) else runif(N) < PI
>     if (all(miss)) miss[1] <- FALSE
>     d <- data.frame(X = X, Y = Y); d$X[miss] <- NA
>     P <- model.matrix(~ Y, data = d)
>     est <- numeric(M)
>     for (j in seq_len(M)) {
>       dd <- d; dd$X[is.na(d$X)] <- impute_norm_draw(d$X, P)
>       est[j] <- unname(coef(lm(Y ~ X + Xsq,
>                                data = transform(dd, Xsq = X^2)))["Xsq"])
>     }
>     k[rep] <- 1 - mean(est) / b2
>   }
>   c(kappa = mean(k), mcse = sd(k) / sqrt(reps))
> }
> CONFIGS <- list(
>   list(l = "base            b1=0.3 b2=0.4  s=1.0", b1 = 0.3, b2 = 0.4,  s = 1.0),
>   list(l = "no linear term  b1=0.0 b2=0.4  s=1.0", b1 = 0.0, b2 = 0.4,  s = 1.0),
>   list(l = "strong linear   b1=1.0 b2=0.4  s=1.0", b1 = 1.0, b2 = 0.4,  s = 1.0),
>   list(l = "linear dominant b1=1.5 b2=0.1  s=1.0", b1 = 1.5, b2 = 0.1,  s = 1.0),
>   list(l = "square dominant b1=0.1 b2=1.5  s=1.0", b1 = 0.1, b2 = 1.5,  s = 1.0),
>   list(l = "low noise       b1=0.3 b2=0.4  s=0.5", b1 = 0.3, b2 = 0.4,  s = 0.5),
>   list(l = "S2 spread       b1=1.2 b2=0.5  s=1.0", b1 = 1.2, b2 = 0.5,  s = 1.0),
>   list(l = "S3 spread       b1=0.5 b2=0.5  s=0.3", b1 = 0.5, b2 = 0.5,  s = 0.3),
>   # discriminating pair: rho^2 ranks A above B, r ranks B above A
>   list(l = "A1 discriminating b1=0.6 b2=0.2 s=2.0", b1 = 0.6, b2 = 0.2, s = 2.0),
>   list(l = "B1 discriminating b1=0.3 b2=1.2 s=0.5", b1 = 0.3, b2 = 1.2, s = 0.5)
> )
> cat(sprintf("MAR on Y (logistic, slope %.1f), pi = %.2f, N = %.0e, %d reps\n\n",
>             GAMMA1, PI, N, REPS))
MAR on Y (logistic, slope 0.7), pi = 0.40, N = 5e+05, 24 reps

> source("R/simulation_functions.R")
> set.seed(20260801L)
> B1 <- 0.3
> B2 <- 0.4
> SIG <- 1.0
> GAMMA1 <- 0.7
> NS  <- c(50, 100, 200, 400, 800)
> PIS <- c(0.20, 0.40)
> R   <- 1000L
> M   <- 20L
> b2_fit <- function(y, x) {
>   X <- cbind(1, x, x^2)
>   q <- qr(X)
>   b <- qr.coef(q, y)
>   r <- y - X %*% b
>   n <- length(y); p <- 3L
>   s2 <- sum(r^2) / (n - p)
>   v  <- s2 * chol2inv(qr.R(q))[3, 3]
>   c(est = unname(b[3]), se = sqrt(v))
> }
> mar_intercept <- function(target, n = 2e5) {
>   x <- rnorm(n); y <- B1 * x + B2 * x^2 + rnorm(n, sd = SIG)
>   z <- as.numeric(scale(y))
>   uniroot(function(g0) mean(plogis(g0 + GAMMA1 * z)) - target, c(-12, 12))$root
> }
> G0 <- vapply(PIS, mar_intercept, numeric(1))
> mi_arm <- function(y, x, jav) {
>   obs <- !is.na(x)
>   P   <- cbind(1, y)
>   Q <- numeric(M); U <- numeric(M)
>   w  <- x^2                                  # NA wherever x is
>   for (j in seq_len(M)) {
>     xj <- x
>     d1 <- blin_draw(x[obs], P[obs, , drop = FALSE])
>     xj[!obs] <- P[!obs, , drop = FALSE] %*% d1$beta +
>                 d1$sigma * rnorm(sum(!obs))
>     if (jav) {
>       wj <- w
>       d2 <- blin_draw(w[obs], P[obs, , drop = FALSE])
>       wj[!obs] <- P[!obs, , drop = FALSE] %*% d2$beta +
>                   d2$sigma * rnorm(sum(!obs))
>       X <- cbind(1, xj, wj)
>       q <- qr(X); b <- qr.coef(q, y); r <- y - X %*% b
>       s2 <- sum(r^2) / (length(y) - 3L)
>       Q[j] <- unname(b[3]); U[j] <- s2 * chol2inv(qr.R(q))[3, 3]
>     } else {
>       f <- b2_fit(y, xj)
>       Q[j] <- f["est"]; U[j] <- f["se"]^2
>     }
>   }
>   pool_rubin(Q, U, df_com = length(y) - 3L, true = B2)
> }

> gh <- function(n) {
>   k <- 1:(n - 1)
>   J <- matrix(0, n, n)
>   J[cbind(k, k + 1)] <- sqrt(k); J[cbind(k + 1, k)] <- sqrt(k)
>   e <- eigen(J, symmetric = TRUE)
>   list(x = rev(e$values), w = rev(e$vectors[1, ]^2))
> }
> build <- function(b1, b2, sg, b0 = 0, nq = 16) {
>   Q <- gh(nq)
>   Yf <- function(x, e) b0 + b1 * x + b2 * x^2 + e
>   EE <- function(f) {
>     s <- 0
>     for (i in seq_along(Q$x)) for (j in seq_along(Q$x))
>       s <- s + Q$w[i] * Q$w[j] * f(Q$x[i], sg * Q$x[j])
>     s
>   }
>   EY   <- EE(function(x, e) Yf(x, e))
>   varY <- EE(function(x, e) Yf(x, e)^2) - EY^2
>   gam  <- EE(function(x, e) x * Yf(x, e)) / varY
>   alp  <- -gam * EY
>   tau2 <- 1 - gam^2 * varY
>   Ec <- function(pz, py) EE(function(x, e) x^pz * Yf(x, e)^py)
>   Ei <- function(pz, py) {
>     s <- 0
>     for (i in seq_along(Q$x)) for (j in seq_along(Q$x)) for (k in seq_along(Q$x)) {
>       y <- Yf(Q$x[i], sg * Q$x[j])
>       z <- alp + gam * y + sqrt(max(tau2, 0)) * Q$x[k]
>       s <- s + Q$w[i] * Q$w[j] * Q$w[k] * z^pz * y^py
>     }
>     s
>   }
>   Gm <- function(f) matrix(c(f(0, 0), f(1, 0), f(2, 0),
>                              f(1, 0), f(2, 0), f(3, 0),
>                              f(2, 0), f(3, 0), f(4, 0)), 3, 3)
>   wv <- function(f) c(f(0, 1), f(1, 1), f(2, 1))
>   list(G = Gm(Ec), Gi = Gm(Ei), om = wv(Ec), omi = wv(Ei), b2 = b2,
>        Ec = Ec, Ei = Ei)
> }
> kappa_of <- function(M) function(p) {
>   A <- (1 - p) * M$G + p * M$Gi
>   r <- (1 - p) * M$om + p * M$omi
>   1 - solve(A, r)[3] / M$b2
> }

> source("R/simulation_functions.R")
> set.seed(20260801L)
> N <- 5e5
> REPS <- 6L
> M <- 5L
> PI <- 0.40
> lambda_of <- function(b1, b2, sig) b1^2 / (b1^2 + 2 * b2^2 + sig^2)
> kappa_at <- function(b1, b2, sig, reps = REPS) {
>   k <- numeric(reps)
>   for (r in seq_len(reps)) {
>     X <- rnorm(N)
>     Y <- b1 * X + b2 * X^2 + rnorm(N, sd = sig)
>     d <- data.frame(X = X, Y = Y)
>     d$X[runif(N) < PI] <- NA
>     P <- model.matrix(~ Y, data = d)
>     est <- numeric(M)
>     for (j in seq_len(M)) {
>       dd <- d; dd$X[is.na(d$X)] <- impute_norm_draw(d$X, P)
>       est[j] <- unname(coef(lm(Y ~ X + Xsq,
>                                data = transform(dd, Xsq = X^2)))["Xsq"])
>     }
>     k[r] <- 1 - mean(est) / b2
>   }
>   c(kappa = mean(k), mcse = sd(k) / sqrt(reps))
> }
> run <- function(label, group, b1, b2, sig) {
>   r <- kappa_at(b1, b2, sig)
>   lam <- lambda_of(b1, b2, sig)
>   cat(sprintf("  %-26s lambda %.4f   kappa %.4f (%.4f)   c = kappa/pi %.4f\n",
>               label, lam, r["kappa"], r["mcse"], r["kappa"] / PI))
>   data.frame(label = label, group = group, b1 = b1, b2 = b2, sigma = sig,
>              lambda = lam, kappa = unname(r["kappa"]), mcse = unname(r["mcse"]),
>              c = unname(r["kappa"]) / PI, N = N, reps = REPS,
>              stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
> }
> rows <- list()
> cat("--- sweep in b1 (b2 = 0.4, sigma = 1): the shape of c against lambda ---\n")
--- sweep in b1 (b2 = 0.4, sigma = 1): the shape of c against lambda ---

> source("R/simulation_functions.R")
> set.seed(20260801L)
> B0 <- 0.0
> B1 <- 0.3
> B2 <- 0.4
> SIG <- 1.0
> GAMMA1 <- 0.7
> gen <- function(n) {
>   X <- rnorm(n)
>   Y <- B0 + B1 * X + B2 * X^2 + rnorm(n, sd = SIG)
>   data.frame(X = X, Y = Y)
> }
> mar_intercept <- function(target, n = 2e5) {
>   d <- gen(n); z <- as.numeric(scale(d$Y))
>   f <- function(g0) mean(plogis(g0 + GAMMA1 * z)) - target
>   uniroot(f, c(-12, 12))$root
> }
> drop_mar <- function(d, g0) {
>   z <- as.numeric(scale(d$Y))
>   miss <- runif(nrow(d)) < plogis(g0 + GAMMA1 * z)
>   d$X[miss] <- NA
>   d
> }
> drop_mcar <- function(d, rate) {
>   d$X[runif(nrow(d)) < rate] <- NA
>   d
> }
> b2_of <- function(fit) unname(coef(fit)["Xsq"])
> arm_full <- function(d) b2_of(lm(Y ~ X + Xsq, data = transform(d, Xsq = X^2)))
> arm_listwise <- function(d) {
>   o <- d[!is.na(d$X), ]
>   b2_of(lm(Y ~ X + Xsq, data = transform(o, Xsq = X^2)))
> }
> arm_naive <- function(d, m = 5L) {
>   P <- model.matrix(~ Y, data = d)
>   est <- numeric(m)
>   for (j in seq_len(m)) {
>     dd <- d
>     dd$X[is.na(d$X)] <- impute_norm_draw(d$X, P)
>     est[j] <- b2_of(lm(Y ~ X + Xsq, data = transform(dd, Xsq = X^2)))
>   }
>   mean(est)
> }
> arm_jav <- function(d, m = 5L) {
>   d$W <- d$X^2                      # NA wherever X is
>   P <- model.matrix(~ Y, data = d)
>   est <- numeric(m)
>   for (j in seq_len(m)) {
>     dd <- d
>     dd$X[is.na(d$X)] <- impute_norm_draw(d$X, P)
>     dd$W[is.na(d$W)] <- impute_norm_draw(d$W, P)
>     est[j] <- unname(coef(lm(Y ~ X + W, data = dd))["W"])
>   }
>   mean(est)
> }
> N    <- 5e5
> REPS <- 10L
> RATES <- c(0.20, 0.40)
> g0 <- vapply(RATES, mar_intercept, numeric(1))
> cat(sprintf("MAR logistic intercepts: %.4f (20%%), %.4f (40%%)\n", g0[1], g0[2]))
MAR logistic intercepts: -1.5194 (20%), -0.4412 (40%)
> rows <- list()
> for (i in seq_along(RATES)) {
>   rate <- RATES[i]
>   for (mech in c("MAR", "MCAR")) {
>     acc <- matrix(NA_real_, REPS, 4,
>                   dimnames = list(NULL, c("full", "listwise", "naive", "jav")))
>     realised <- numeric(REPS)
>     for (r in seq_len(REPS)) {

> suppressWarnings(suppressMessages(source("R/simulation_functions.R")))
> set.seed(20260725)
> rho1 <- 0.6
> rho2 <- 0.2
> zeta <- atanh(rho1) - atanh(rho2)
> pi_t <- 0.40
> m_imp <- 20L
> reps <- 300L
> Ns   <- c(40, 80, 160, 320)
> gen <- function(N) {
>   n1 <- N %/% 2; n2 <- N - n1
>   g  <- rep(c(1, 2), c(n1, n2))
>   rho <- ifelse(g == 1, rho1, rho2)
>   x  <- rnorm(N)
>   y  <- rho * x + sqrt(1 - rho^2) * rnorm(N)   # X,Y ~ BVN(0,1,rho_g)
>   data.frame(X = x, Y = y, G = g)
> }
> yref <- rnorm(2e5)
> g0 <- uniroot(function(a) mean(plogis(a + 0.7 * yref)) - pi_t, c(-20, 20))$root
> impose <- function(d) { d$X[runif(nrow(d)) < plogis(g0 + 0.7 * d$Y)] <- NA; d }
> zdiff <- function(d) {
>   r1 <- suppressWarnings(cor(d$X[d$G == 1], d$Y[d$G == 1], use = "complete.obs"))
>   r2 <- suppressWarnings(cor(d$X[d$G == 2], d$Y[d$G == 2], use = "complete.obs"))
>   n1 <- sum(d$G == 1 & !is.na(d$X)); n2 <- sum(d$G == 2 & !is.na(d$X))
>   if (n1 < 5 || n2 < 5 || abs(r1) >= 1 || abs(r2) >= 1) return(NULL)
>   est <- atanh(r1) - atanh(r2)
>   se  <- sqrt(1/(n1 - 3) + 1/(n2 - 3))
>   c(est = est, se = se)
> }
> wald <- function(est, se, true) {
>   est <- unname(est); se <- unname(se)
>   lo <- est - 1.96 * se; hi <- est + 1.96 * se
>   c(est = est, covered = as.numeric(true >= lo & true <= hi),
>     reject = as.numeric(lo > 0 | hi < 0))
> }
> mi_arm <- function(dm, congenial) {
>   Q <- U <- numeric(m_imp)
>   for (j in seq_len(m_imp)) {
>     d <- dm
>     if (congenial) {
>       for (gg in 1:2) {
>         idx <- d$G == gg
>         if (any(is.na(d$X[idx]))) {
>           P <- model.matrix(~ Y, data = d[idx, ])
>           d$X[idx][is.na(dm$X[idx])] <- impute_norm_draw(dm$X[idx], P)
>         }
>       }
>     } else {
>       P <- model.matrix(~ Y + factor(G), data = d)   # group MAIN EFFECT only
>       d$X[is.na(dm$X)] <- impute_norm_draw(dm$X, P)
>     }
>     v <- zdiff(d); if (is.null(v)) return(NULL)
>     Q[j] <- v["est"]; U[j] <- v["se"]^2
>   }
>   pool_rubin(Q, U, df_com = nrow(dm) - 6, true = zeta)
> }
> rows <- list()
> k <- 0L
> for (N in Ns) {
>   acc <- list(full = c(), listw = c(), naive = c(), cong = c())
>   cov <- list(full = c(), listw = c(), naive = c(), cong = c())
>   for (r in seq_len(reps)) {
>     d0 <- gen(N); dm <- impose(d0)
>     vf <- zdiff(d0)
>     if (!is.null(vf)) { w <- wald(vf["est"], vf["se"], zeta)
>       acc$full <- c(acc$full, w["est"]); cov$full <- c(cov$full, w["covered"]) }
>     vl <- zdiff(dm)
>     if (!is.null(vl)) { w <- wald(vl["est"], vl["se"], zeta)
>       acc$listw <- c(acc$listw, w["est"]); cov$listw <- c(cov$listw, w["covered"]) }
>     vn <- tryCatch(mi_arm(dm, congenial = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
>     if (!is.null(vn)) { acc$naive <- c(acc$naive, vn["est"])
>       cov$naive <- c(cov$naive, vn["covered"]) }
>     vc <- tryCatch(mi_arm(dm, congenial = TRUE), error = function(e) NULL)
>     if (!is.null(vc)) { acc$cong <- c(acc$cong, vc["est"])
>       cov$cong <- c(cov$cong, vc["covered"]) }
>   }
>   for (arm in names(acc)) {
>     k <- k + 1L; n <- length(acc[[arm]])
>     rows[[k]] <- data.frame(N = N, arm = arm, n_valid = n,
>       bias_z = mean(acc[[arm]]) - zeta,
>       mcse   = sd(acc[[arm]])/sqrt(n),
>       coverage = mean(cov[[arm]]))
>   }
>   cat(sprintf("N=%d done\n", N))
> }

File paths

1 data path in the code does not work in the repository as deposited. We pointed it to where the file is, so the code could run: # RECORDED OUTPUT -- regenerated by scripts/p36_record_verify.py to scripts/p36_record_verify.py (in p36_record_verify.py). The code should be changed, because as written it does not find the file. The code reads files that are only inside p36imp_osf_bundle_paper1_2026-10-27_2044_56f9ba37.zip, p36p2_osf-deposit_2026-11-09_1850_9c8b71dc.zip, p36p3_osf-deposit_2026-11-12_1303_beb9d6d2.zip, p36p2_osf-deposit_2026-11-14_2210_62c85d9d.zip, p36p3_osf-deposit_2026-11-16_0651_efa5c1da.zip, p36imp_osf_bundle_20261007_v5.zip, and no script unpacks them. We unpacked them in their folder before the run. So that others can run the code as deposited, start the code with a line that unpacks them (such as zipfile.ZipFile("p36imp_osf_bundle_paper1_2026-10-27_2044_56f9ba37.zip").extractall() in Python), or upload the files unpacked.

Files the deposit does not hold

The scripts that did not run through read 2 data files that are not in the deposit, and no script of the deposit writes: drug_consumption.data, p36_p3g22v_spi_es_trust.csv.

Execution

The Python code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 91 scripts: 0 ran without error, 0 errored, 0 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse, and 0 are written for Python 2 and not run. 1 file was not run on its own, because other files import it: p36_p2g22v_engine.py (by p36_p2g22v_B_spread.py). Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions (e.g. in a requirements.txt). 90 scripts were not started, or stopped early, because the time for all scripts together had run out. The checks before this one had left 0 sec before the time limit, too little to copy the repository, install its packages and run its scripts (at least 15 min), so none of that was done.

os.chdir() in the code

1 script calls os.chdir(). This is bad practice: it hardcodes where the code must run (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine) and breaks the moment the code is run anywhere else. To run the code we replaced these calls with pass. Any such script that then ran is reproducible only after ignoring an os.chdir() that should not have been in the code and needs to be fixed.

Ethics Approval Check

An ethics approval statement was detected, based on the following text:

Ethics approval.

Power Analysis Check

No power analyses were detected.

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen’s d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

StatCheck

No t-tests or F-tests detected.

The accuracy of StatCheck has only been validated for t-tests and F-tests.
